claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch on a narrow basis because aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, rollout is limited and reversible, and the remaining model-card weakness can be handled through explicit documented limitation and active monitoring rather than being treated as fully resolved.
decision_criteria: If admissible evidence shows the material limitation was explicitly disclosed before launch, the narrow certification rationale becomes materially stronger.
If admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance that specifically covers the exposed developer-support migration segment, the policy predicate could also be satisfied.
If neither disclosure nor approved risk acceptance exists, certification is not policy-supported because the affected use case remains exposed.
Aggregate readiness, lack of severity-one incidents, low initial percentage, rollback, and monitoring are supportive context but are not sufficient by themselves under the stated policy.
evidence_requests: Final approved model card or equivalent launch artifact showing the material limitation is explicitly disclosed for the named launch use case.
Approved risk acceptance that specifically addresses developer-support migration exposure, if the organization intends to rely on risk acceptance instead of disclosure.
Launch approval record or certification memo showing whether certification was conditioned on disclosure and confirming that condition was satisfied before launch.
specific_concerns: The affected developer-support migration segment remains exposed in the 7% rollout because the gate does not exclude it.
The only risk acceptance in the record is an unsigned draft and it does not address the exposed developer-support migration segment.
Policy expressly says rollout controls and monitoring do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
The packet supports a need for disclosure or approved risk acceptance, but does not provide admissible evidence that the required disclosure has actually been made before launch.
The recommendation to certify depends on a future or implied documentation step that is not itself evidenced in the record.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant on the existing record, rather than only potentially compliant if required disclosure is actually included before launch.
That rollout controls materially mitigate the weakness enough to support certification absent evidence of exclusion of the affected segment or approved risk acceptance.
That the narrow certification position is fully evidentially supported, as opposed to conditionally supportable pending proof of disclosure.
